After the city fell in June 1535 he was tortured and executed in January 1536; the iron cages that displayed the bodies still hang from the tower of St Lambert’s Church. Mainstream Anabaptists such as Menno Simons repudiated the episode.
keyIdeas: Armed resistance to hasten the end

people.name: Manuel Lacunza
people.summary: Chilean Jesuit who, exiled to Imola in Italy after the suppression of the Jesuits in Spanish America (1767), wrote La venida del Mesías en gloria y majestad under the pen-name "Juan Josafat Ben-Ezra". Published in 1812 and placed on the Index in 1824, it argued for a future, literal millennial reign of Christ and a restoration of Israel. Edward Irving’s English translation (1827) fed directly into the British prophetic revival from which dispensationalism emerged, a notable Latin American contribution to modern premillennialism.
keyIdeas: Future conversion and restoration of Israel

works.title: Against Heresies (Adversus Haereses)
works.summary: Five-book refutation of Gnostic systems, setting out the rule of faith, apostolic succession, recapitulation in Christ and, in Book 5, a literal earthly kingdom of the righteous after the resurrection.
works.significance: The fullest second-century statement of catholic theology; Book 5 is the classic early witness to chiliasm.

works.title: Dialogue with Trypho
works.summary: Justin’s record of a debate with a Jewish teacher about the fulfilment of the Hebrew Scriptures in Christ.
works.significance: Earliest extended Christian–Jewish dialogue; chapters 80–81 affirm a thousand-year kingdom in a rebuilt Jerusalem while admitting that some orthodox Christians disagree.

works.title: Against Marcion
works.summary: Five-book refutation of Marcion’s separation of the God of the Old Testament from the Father of Jesus.
works.significance: Defends the unity of the Testaments; Book 3.24 affirms an earthly kingdom for a thousand years in a heavenly Jerusalem.

works.title: On First Principles (De Principiis / Peri Archon)
works.summary: The first systematic Christian theology, covering God, creation, rational beings, free will, Scripture and the end.
works.significance: Pioneered allegorical exegesis and spiritual eschatology; criticised literal millenarian hopes (2.11.2).

works.title: Ecclesiastical History
works.summary: Ten-book history of the Church from Christ to Constantine, quoting many otherwise lost sources.
works.significance: Primary source for Papias, the Montanists and early controversies; transmits the anti-chiliast judgement of the Constantinian church.

works.title: The City of God (De Civitate Dei)
works.summary: Twenty-two books contrasting the earthly city founded on love of self with the heavenly city founded on love of God, written after the sack of Rome (410).
works.significance: Book 20 established the amillennial reading of Revelation 20 (the millennium as the age of the Church) that dominated Western theology for over a millennium; Book 19 shaped just-war and church–state thought.

works.title: Book of Rules (Liber Regularum)
works.summary: Seven hermeneutical rules for interpreting Scripture’s figures, including the "bipartite body" of the Church.
works.significance: First Latin hermeneutics manual; Augustine summarised it in On Christian Doctrine 3, transmitting a non-chronological reading of Revelation.

works.title: Exposition on the Apocalypse (Expositio in Apocalypsim)
works.summary: Joachim’s major commentary reading Revelation as a map of the whole history of the Church, structured by patterns of concordance between the Testaments and culminating in a coming age of the Spirit.
works.significance: With the Liber de Concordia and Psalterium decem chordarum, it launched the Joachite tradition of historical-prophetic reading that inspired Spiritual Franciscans and later reformers.

works.title: Augsburg Confession (Confessio Augustana)
works.summary: Twenty-eight articles presented by Lutheran princes to Emperor Charles V at the Diet of Augsburg, drafted by Philip Melanchthon.
works.significance: Founding confession of Lutheranism; Article XVII rejects chiliasm, Article XVI permits Christians to hold office and wage just wars, Article X affirms the true presence in the Supper.

works.title: Institutes of the Christian Religion
works.summary: Calvin’s systematic theology, first published 1536 and expanded to its final four-book form in 1559.
works.significance: The most influential Reformed theology; treats the sacraments and Supper (4.14–18), church government (4.3–12) and civil government (4.20), and dismisses chiliasm (3.25.5).

works.title: A History of the Work of Redemption
works.summary: Thirty sermons preached in Northampton in 1739 and published posthumously, tracing redemption from the Fall to the end of the world.
works.significance: Classic statement of postmillennial optimism: the gospel’s progressive triumph through revival before Christ’s return.

works.title: Apology and Defence
works.summary: William Miller’s account, written after the Great Disappointment, of how his Bible study led him to expect Christ’s return around 1843–44.
works.significance: Key primary source for the Millerite movement and its aftermath.

works.title: The Hopes of the Church of God in Connexion with the Destiny of the Jews and the Nations
works.summary: Lectures delivered by Darby in Geneva in 1840 setting out a distinction between God’s heavenly people (the Church) and earthly people (Israel).
works.significance: An early systematic statement of the Israel–Church distinction and the Church’s heavenly hope that underlie dispensationalism.

works.title: The Scofield Reference Bible
works.summary: King James Bible with Cyrus Scofield’s headings, cross-references and notes, published by Oxford University Press (revised 1917).
works.significance: Carried dispensational premillennialism into millions of homes and Bible institutes; arguably the most influential single vehicle of the doctrine.

works.title: The Parables of the Kingdom
works.summary: Dodd’s study arguing that Jesus’ parables announce the kingdom as already present in his ministry.

works.title: The Presence of the Future
works.summary: Revised edition of Ladd’s Jesus and the Kingdom (1964), arguing that the kingdom is God’s dynamic reign, inaugurated in Jesus and consummated at his return.
works.significance: Brought inaugurated ("already/not yet") eschatology into the evangelical mainstream.

works.title: Sermon to the Princes (Fürstenpredigt)
works.summary: Thomas Müntzer’s exposition of Daniel 2 preached before Duke John of Saxony at Allstedt, 13 July 1524.
works.significance: Urged the princes to wield the sword against the godless in the last days; a key text of revolutionary apocalypticism before the Peasants’ War.

quotes.text: The days will come, in which vines shall grow, each having ten thousand branches, and in each branch ten thousand twigs, and in each true twig ten thousand shoots, and in each one of the shoots ten thousand clusters, and on every one of the clusters ten thousand grapes.
quotes.citation: Irenaeus, Against Heresies 5.33.3 (ANF vol. 1), reporting a saying the elders who saw John attributed to the Lord, also attested by Papias

quotes.text: But I and others, who are right-minded Christians on all points, are assured that there will be a resurrection of the dead, and a thousand years in Jerusalem, which will then be built, adorned, and enlarged, as the prophets Ezekiel and Isaiah and others declare.
quotes.citation: Justin Martyr, Dialogue with Trypho 80 (ANF vol. 1)

quotes.text: We do confess that a kingdom is promised to us upon the earth ... inasmuch as it will be after the resurrection for a thousand years in the divinely-built city of Jerusalem.

Certain persons, then, refusing the labour of thinking, and adopting a superficial view of the letter of the law ... are of opinion that the fulfilment of the promises of the future are to be looked for in bodily pleasure and luxury.
To these belong his statement that there will be a period of some thousand years after the resurrection of the dead, and that the kingdom of Christ will be set up in material form on this very earth.
quotes.citation: Eusebius, Ecclesiastical History 3.39.12 (NPNF 2nd ser. vol. 1, tr. McGiffert)

quotes.text: For he appears to have been of very limited understanding, as one can see from his discourses.
quotes.citation: Eusebius, Ecclesiastical History 3.39.13 (NPNF 2nd ser. vol. 1, tr. McGiffert), on Papias

quotes.text: And this opinion would not be objectionable, if it were believed that the joys of the saints in that Sabbath shall be spiritual, and consequent on the presence of God; for I myself, too, once held this opinion.
quotes.citation: Augustine, City of God 20.7 (NPNF 1st ser. vol. 2, tr. Dods)

quotes.text: Therefore the Church even now is the kingdom of Christ, and the kingdom of heaven.
quotes.citation: Augustine, City of God 20.9 (NPNF 1st ser. vol. 2, tr. Dods)

quotes.text: Joachim taught that history unfolds in three states (status): the age of the Father under the law, lived by the married; the age of the Son under grace, lived by the clergy; and a coming age of the Holy Spirit, of fuller spiritual understanding and contemplative liberty, lived by monks.
quotes.citation: Paraphrase of Joachim of Fiore, Liber de Concordia and Expositio in Apocalypsim (c.1184–1200); see Reeves, Joachim of Fiore and the Prophetic Future (1976)

quotes.text: Müntzer told the Saxon princes that the stone "cut without hands" of Daniel 2 was about to crush the kingdoms of the world, and that if the princes would not use their sword to root out the godless, it would be taken from them.
quotes.citation: Paraphrase of Thomas Müntzer, Sermon to the Princes (Allstedt, 13 July 1524)

quotes.text: They condemn also others who are now spreading certain Jewish opinions, that before the resurrection of the dead the godly shall take possession of the kingdom of the world, the ungodly being everywhere suppressed.
quotes.citation: Augsburg Confession (1530), Article XVII (tr. in Schaff, Creeds of Christendom vol. 3 / Triglot Concordia)

quotes.text: Shortly after arose the Chiliasts, who limited the reign of Christ to a thousand years. Now their fiction is too puerile to need or to deserve refutation.
quotes.citation: Calvin, Institutes of the Christian Religion 3.25.5 (tr. Henry Beveridge, 1845)

quotes.text: Edwards argued that through successive outpourings of the Spirit the gospel would spread over the whole earth, overthrowing Satan’s kingdoms (which he identified with heathenism, Islam and the papacy), so that a long era of peace, learning and holiness would precede Christ’s final return.
quotes.citation: Paraphrase of Jonathan Edwards, A History of the Work of Redemption (preached 1739, publ. 1774), Period III

quotes.text: I was thus brought, in 1818, at the close of my two years’ study of the Scriptures, to the solemn conclusion, that in about twenty-five years from that time all the affairs of our present state would be wound up.
quotes.citation: William Miller, Apology and Defence (Boston: J. V. Himes, 1845)

quotes.text: Darby taught that the Church is a heavenly people with a heavenly calling, distinct from Israel, God’s earthly people; the prophecies of an earthly kingdom belong to Israel, and the Church’s proper hope is to be caught up to meet Christ before God resumes his dealings with Israel.
quotes.citation: Paraphrase of J. N. Darby, The Hopes of the Church of God (Geneva lectures, 1840)

quotes.text: A dispensation is a period of time during which man is tested in respect of obedience to some specific revelation of the will of God. Seven such dispensations are distinguished in Scripture.
quotes.citation: Scofield Reference Bible (Oxford, 1909), note on Genesis 1:28

quotes.text: Dodd argued that in Jesus’ preaching the kingdom of God is not a future hope but a present fact: the eschaton has entered history in the ministry, death and resurrection of Jesus, and the parables summon hearers to decide in that moment of crisis.
quotes.citation: Paraphrase of C. H. Dodd, The Parables of the Kingdom (1935), chs. 2–3

quotes.text: Ladd argued that the kingdom of God is God’s dynamic reign, which has invaded this age in Jesus without yet ending it: the age to come has arrived in fulfilment before its consummation, so believers live "between the times".
quotes.citation: Paraphrase of George Eldon Ladd, The Presence of the Future (1974), chs. 1 and 6
